meta.title: Everyscreen: see every screen while your agent tests it
meta.description: Everyscreen opens your web app in real device frames at their true size, runs your tests on all of them at once, and gives your agent one short line per device.

hero.title: See every screen while your agent tests it.
hero.subtitle: Everyscreen is open source and runs on your machine. It opens your app in real device frames at their true size, runs your tests on all of them at once, and gives your agent one short line per device.

tools.intro: Works with the agents and test tools you already use.

command-section.title: One command. Every screen answers.
command-section.subtitle: Your agent sends one step. Every device runs it at once and answers in one line, so a full sweep costs a few lines of context, not a stack of screenshots.

checks.subtitle: Every step runs six checks on every device. Each finding pops a toast in the dashboard and lands in the run report.

estimates.title: See how hard each screen works.

faq.title: Questions
faq.subtitle: Something missing? Open an issue on GitHub.

frameworks.question: Which frameworks does it work with?
frameworks.answer: Any web app that runs at a URL: React, Vue, Svelte, Next.js, Expo web or plain HTML. Each frame opens your dev server at its own size.

safari.question: Is the iPhone frame running real Safari?
safari.answer: No. It runs WebKit through Playwright with the iPhone's screen size, pixel ratio and touch, and the safe-area check uses the iPhone's notch and home bar. That is close to Safari, not the same. Live video is Chromium only; WebKit and Firefox frames update after each step.

numbers.question: Are the FPS and CPU numbers real?
numbers.answer: They are estimates from the browser on your machine, with the CPU slowed down per device. Good for spotting a slow screen, not for a lab benchmark.

privacy.question: Does my code leave my machine?
privacy.answer: Not with the free tool. The hub and the dashboard run on 127.0.0.1. Cloud only runs what your CI sends it.

agents.question: Which agents can drive it?
agents.answer: Any agent that can run a shell command, such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. A Claude Code skill ships with it.

cloud.question: What does Cloud add?
cloud.answer: A run on every pull request in a separate environment, a live preview link with every device frame, and the failure proof posted on the PR.

closing.title: Open every screen at once.
